text: Writing clean code is an important skill for every programmer. Clean code is easy to read and understand, even for someone who did not write it. One key idea is using clear naming conventions, so variables and functions have meaningful names. For example, a function called "calculateTotal" is much better than one called "calc". Another important point is keeping functions small and focused on one task. This makes the code easier to test and reuse. Finally, clean code is easier to maintain. When you need to fix a bug or add a feature later, well-organized code saves you time and reduces mistakes.
